A resource has a path: organization, then workspace, then project, then whatever sits under those. A grant covers a path and everything below it. One check asks whether some grant the caller holds covers the target and admits the verb — and org-wide access, one workspace, an invite-only project, and a narrowed credential handed to an agent all fall out of that with no special case for any of them.
A resource tree, not a pile of flags
A resume is a PDF, DOC or DOCX file.
A resume is at most 10 MB.

A retained record — a relationship, a transaction, the assessment behind a case, a refusal — carries its own five-year clock, started by the end of the relationship, by the occasional transaction, or by the refusal itself. Disposal runs daily and proves what it destroyed before it reports it. Alerts and case timelines are durable, and are not on that clock.
A rising timestamp compresses as deltas. A repeated label compresses as a dictionary. A general-purpose compressor runs over whatever is left.
A role is granted at a place — an organization, a workspace under it, a single project. The token carries the one that applies to the request, so your service decides without asking us anything.
A row in a column store rather than a series in a store of its own.
A row is a run, as of its date.

A row marked {ran} is a number produced by our own harness, and the link goes to the run. A row marked {published} is each vendor’s own claim, taken from the page linked and dated the day it was read — we relay those, we did not verify them, and they are their numbers and not ours. Where a vendor has not published something the cell says {unpublished} rather than being left blank, because a blank reads as zero.
A row store reads the whole row to answer a question about two of its fields. A column store reads the two.
A run is a record, not a goroutine. Step state is written down as it goes, so a crash, a deploy or a rescheduled pod resumes where it stopped rather than starting over or losing the run.
A run that survives the restart
A run’s reproducible record, and the rules that govern it.
A sales rep if you want one.

A sandbox is what an agent needs to run a command. What it costs to keep an agent that is doing nothing is {dormant}, and what a running agent holds is {live}. The three are separate measurements with separate commands and they do not add up into a single number.
A sandbox that runs a shell, cold
A saved query you want watched rather than looked at. Same definition as the widget beside it, kept in one place so the alert and the chart cannot disagree.

A screen, a way to watch it, and the tools the model drives it with

A second LoCoMo harness, in Go, with no language model anywhere in it: lexical retrieval and a fixed extractive reader, with retrieval scoped to the person a question names, against a flat index. Its numbers are on their own scale, not the engine’s.
A second factor is an authenticator app, a code by SMS or email, or a passkey. Adding or dropping one signs the account out of every other browser.

A second factor is an authenticator app, or a code by SMS or email, with recovery codes shown once and stored hashed. Adding one, removing one, or changing which is preferred drops every other session and clears the remember-me window. A session that outlives the change is the same as not having made it.
A secret is a value under a path, a name and an environment, inside one organization. That is the whole model.

A private registry for your container images at oci.hanzo.ai. It serves the OCI distribution API, so docker, podman, buildkit, skopeo and crane already know how to talk to it — and the credential is a short-lived token minted by your Hanzo IAM login, not a password living in a dockerconfigjson secret.
A probability for every option, and no text written.
A probability is advice. Your policy, written as code, keeps the authority — and a person signs where it says one must.

A produce whose batch chain does not line up is refused with INVALID_RECORD instead of being written and discovered later by a consumer that cannot get past it. The scan that recovers a partition's bounds is capped, so a damaged topic degrades rather than stalls.
A product holds the description; a variant holds the size, the colour and the price. Stock is tracked on the variant, which is the thing people actually buy.

A provider whose response we do not parse refuses rather than answering. Two of them used to return approved without reading the reply — one for any response that was not an error, the other including a rejected document. Anything gating on that would have admitted an unverified person, so both now refuse until the parsing is written.

A public HTTPS URL for something running on your laptop. The port stays bound to localhost and the Hanzo fabric carries the traffic to it, so nothing is listening on whatever network the machine is sitting on.
A public URL for a local port

A quarter of LoCoMo’s questions are adversarial: they ask about something the conversation never said, and the right answer is to decline. Scoping retrieval to the person a question names scores {ours} on the {n} of them against the flat index’s {theirs}, because an assertion about the wrong person is not retrieved for the right one.
A question and its paraphrase, mean |Δp| over {n} pairs
A queue per GPU, plus a shared any-GPU lane
A quiet song for the walk home
A rating or report you send us may be used to improve Hanzo. A rating alone does not allow training on the whole conversation.
A reader that walks the buffer in place allocates nothing per message, so there is no garbage to collect and no pause to tune away later.
A real xterm.js terminal with 10k lines of scrollback, true colour and a cursor that blinks. Type in it, page through it, resize it.
A real-time map of every model, agent, and tool call. Trace any request from edge to GPU.
A record is written once and handed to the subscribers already attached to it. The work is the number of people watching, not the size of the collection they are watching.
A referral on its own pays nothing; what a qualified referral is worth is this commission. Authors of open source are paid on a separate schedule, described on {royalty}.
A release is an immutable pin of image plus configuration. Roll forward or back to any previous one in a single operation, with a full history of who shipped what.

A render takes minutes, so the call does not wait for it: POST /v1/videos/generations returns a job, GET /v1/videos/{id} reports where it has got to, and /v1/videos/{id}/content hands back the finished MP4. Nothing holds a connection open while a model works.
A replayed refresh token ends the whole chain

A repository name begins with your org, and what a token may do with it is decided by IAM at the moment the token is minted. Adding a teammate is one grant in one place, not a secret copied into a second.
A request can touch a model, a tool, an agent, your memory, a decision and the machine it runs on. Enso is the runtime that decides which.

A request that crosses four services is one trace, and the span that took the time is visible in it. Profiles go a level down to the function. Session replay shows the same failure from the browser's side.

A key is told apart from a token by its prefix, so nothing has to guess what it was handed. Tokens are refused outright if they carry an HMAC signature or no algorithm at all, and a refresh token is single-use — presenting a spent one revokes its whole family rather than the one token.

A freshly built binary is slower the first time it runs, and not slightly: three fresh builds read 202, 210 and 201 ns, and the same three read 123, 125 and 123 ns when run again. The window is 41 ms rather than 25 ms for the same 200,000 spawns, so it is one fixed cost inside the measurement, paid once per binary for first-touch paging and the kernel's signature check on first exec. GPQA-Diamond is four-way multiple choice on settled science. It measures what a pool knows and rewards a router that recognises a hard question; it says nothing about whether the answer is reasoned, whether the model holds up over a long autonomous run, or whether it can use a tool. The routing overhead is real work this table does not score either.

GPQA-Diamond is the hardest subset of GPQA: 198 multiple-choice questions in biology, physics and chemistry, written by domain PhDs and filtered to the ones that other PhDs get right and skilled non-experts get wrong even with the web open. It is a knowledge benchmark rather than an agentic one — one question, one answer, no tools — which is what makes it useful here: it isolates the choice of model from everything else a system does.

A stream captures the subjects you name and keeps them by age, by count or by bytes. A consumer starts at the beginning, at the newest message, at a sequence number or at a wall-clock time, and reads at the original pace or as fast as it can take them.
A study with a baseline and acceptance criteria reviews new results as they arrive. Findings remain drafts until reviewed.

A switch that sits between your checkout and the companies that actually move the money. You integrate once; it speaks to each processor in that processor’s own language. When one declines a payment another would have taken, it retries there instead of handing your customer an error — and changing processors stops being a project.

A table is stored one column at a time, so a query reads only the columns it names. Each column gets a codec suited to what it holds — deltas for a rising timestamp, dictionaries for a repeated label, general compression over the result.
A team of forty wants in
A team that works for you
A team with five AI tools and too many tabs.
A teammate with its own computer
A teammate you can trust with real work.
A tenancy boundary that only exists in a WHERE clause is one bug from being nothing.
A tenant key is derived, not stored
A tenth of the block reward funds AI compute, and a provider's share is scaled by the level of the work it did. No subscription, no seat, nothing billed while a machine sits idle.

A tenth of the block reward is set aside for AI compute. A provider's share is scaled by the level of the work — embeddings and small models, chat-sized models, large and multimodal, training, or specialized compute like proofs.
A thank-you card for the shop, signed by everyone
A token is trusted for what it cryptographically is
A tool an agent can call
A tool is a Python function with a signature. Every Hanzo MCP tool is one too, so an agent gets a shell, a filesystem, a code index and HTTP without you writing wrappers for them.

A tool list is a prompt. Two hundred entries crowd out the work, and a model picks badly among near-duplicates. So each tool here is one noun with a set of verbs: you call fs with read, or exec with run, and the schema tells the model what the verb needs.
A transaction is a set of postings with a source and a destination, and it is rejected unless it balances. Entries are immutable — a correction is another transaction, so history stays true.
A usage record per call and one balance per organization, so spend is attributed where it happened instead of totalled at the end of the month.
A user-agent string cannot tell you whether traffic is a scraper or a customer’s agent doing work it was asked to do. The plane will not read one.
A verified author earns 20% of the metered spend of every deploy built from their repository.
A view fires an event. Knowing someone opened the deck while you are still in the thread is worth more than knowing it on Monday.
A webhook has to prove it is one
A webhook you have to receive. A build a client wants to click through. An OAuth callback that will not accept localhost.
A whole machine when a container is the wrong shape — provisioned on our account or folded in from yours, each one carrying an agent you address directly.
A whole machine, by the second.
A widget names what to select and how to group it. Because it queries the store that already holds your traces, a chart cannot drift from what happened.

A private registry for your container images at oci.hanzo.ai. It serves the OCI distribution API, so docker, podman, buildkit, skopeo and crane already know how to talk to it — and the credential is a short-lived token minted by your Hanzo IAM login, not a password living in a dockerconfigjson secret.
A probability for every option, and no text written.
A probability is advice. Your policy, written as code, keeps the authority — and a person signs where it says one must.

A produce whose batch chain does not line up is refused with INVALID_RECORD instead of being written and discovered later by a consumer that cannot get past it. The scan that recovers a partition's bounds is capped, so a damaged topic degrades rather than stalls.
A product holds the description; a variant holds the size, the colour and the price. Stock is tracked on the variant, which is the thing people actually buy.

A provider whose response we do not parse refuses rather than answering. Two of them used to return approved without reading the reply — one for any response that was not an error, the other including a rejected document. Anything gating on that would have admitted an unverified person, so both now refuse until the parsing is written.

A public HTTPS URL for something running on your laptop. The port stays bound to localhost and the Hanzo fabric carries the traffic to it, so nothing is listening on whatever network the machine is sitting on.
A public URL for a local port

A quarter of LoCoMo’s questions are adversarial: they ask about something the conversation never said, and the right answer is to decline. Scoping retrieval to the person a question names scores {ours} on the {n} of them against the flat index’s {theirs}, because an assertion about the wrong person is not retrieved for the right one.
A question and its paraphrase, mean |Δp| over {n} pairs
A queue per GPU, plus a shared any-GPU lane
A quiet song for the walk home
A rating or report you send us may be used to improve Hanzo. A rating alone does not allow training on the whole conversation.
A reader that walks the buffer in place allocates nothing per message, so there is no garbage to collect and no pause to tune away later.
A real xterm.js terminal with 10k lines of scrollback, true colour and a cursor that blinks. Type in it, page through it, resize it.
A real-time map of every model, agent, and tool call. Trace any request from edge to GPU.
A record is written once and handed to the subscribers already attached to it. The work is the number of people watching, not the size of the collection they are watching.
A referral on its own pays nothing; what a qualified referral is worth is this commission. Authors of open source are paid on a separate schedule, described on {royalty}.
A release is an immutable pin of image plus configuration. Roll forward or back to any previous one in a single operation, with a full history of who shipped what.

A render takes minutes, so the call does not wait for it: POST /v1/videos/generations returns a job, GET /v1/videos/{id} reports where it has got to, and /v1/videos/{id}/content hands back the finished MP4. Nothing holds a connection open while a model works.
A replayed refresh token ends the whole chain

A repository name begins with your org, and what a token may do with it is decided by IAM at the moment the token is minted. Adding a teammate is one grant in one place, not a secret copied into a second.
A request can touch a model, a tool, an agent, your memory, a decision and the machine it runs on. Enso is the runtime that decides which.

A request that crosses four services is one trace, and the span that took the time is visible in it. Profiles go a level down to the function. Session replay shows the same failure from the browser's side.

A completion point needs one snippet from another file, and the file’s imports, definitions and identifiers say which. RepoBench-R gives about twelve candidates per item with one of them correct, in two settings: {first}, the first cross-file line of a file, and {random}, any of them. Python. Retrieval is scored on its own, apart from generation, which is the reason this benchmark is here — it isolates the part a memory is responsible for.
A component is a Python class. Edit it in the browser and the change is live on the next run — no rebuild, no plugin format, no waiting for someone to add the parameter you need.
A connection is a named credential the flow refers to. It is encrypted at rest through Hanzo KMS, and who may touch it is Hanzo IAM's answer, not a second login here.
A consent screen the person has to pass before an app gets a token

A container with a Linux desktop inside it, and a model driving that desktop by screenshot, mouse and keyboard. You watch through a browser and send instructions from the same page. Nothing it does reaches your machine, because the machine it is using is the container.
A context runs JavaScript, which makes it the right primitive for a JavaScript transform. An agent that installs a package or runs a shell gets a microVM instead, which is a separate measurement.
A cron expression, a delay in milliseconds, or a job that repeats on an interval — timezone aware, and held in the store rather than in a process that might restart.
A customer answered, then thanked us
A customer wants a refund for a month they did not use. Draft a reply.
A dashboard is a saved query
A deck, a model and four intros
A decline cascades to a backup rather than to your customer
A delete is announced only to the subscribers whose rule would have let them read the record. Something you were never allowed to see does not reveal itself on the way out.
A demo that does not bill per visitor
A desk with too many plants, as a scene we can walk through
A desktop app that drafts and summarizes without a round trip
A direct referral pays you {share} of Hanzo’s margin on its metered spend, every period it spends. At the default {margin} margin that is {bill} of the bill, and the customer’s price does not change.

A dormant agent is a row on disk. An agent that is {running} still has to hold its place, and the question is what that place costs. Here it is a goroutine: the heap it occupies, the time to start one, and the time to wake a million of them at once. The comparison column is what a platform built on V8 isolates publishes for the same two quantities.

A dormant agent is a row; a running one still has to hold its place. 601 bytes of heap per live agent, 125 ns to spawn one, 107 ms to wake a million — and the three language runtimes that can sit inside one.
A dormant agent is not a running one.
A double-entry ledger for money moving inside your product

A double-entry ledger you post to over HTTP. Money here only ever moves: a posting names a source account, a destination account, an amount and an asset. There is no way to write a debit without its credit, because a one-sided entry is not something the API can express.
A dropped stream reopens with a fresh grant
A failure seen before with nothing changed picks a different action, or escalates. It never replays the loop.
A few of the ones people reach for first. Every parameter and error shape is in the reference.
A first-party Rust kernel DSL targeting CUDA, ROCm, Vulkan and Metal alongside backend-specific implementations.
A security review is part of every Enterprise contract. We answer your questionnaire against the code, and the engineers who wrote it walk your reviewers through it.
A seed fund that backs developer tools
A sensory buffer for the turn, working memory for the session, and a long-term graph of episodic, semantic and procedural memory that survives a restart.
A served-only bridge between Zen 5 and Zen 6, with no public weights. The gateway does not list it now.
A shell is never open by hostname
A short loop to match the header is in the Library.
A short workflow imports the pipeline from hanzoai/ci, so every repo runs the same steps from one definition. Tests run first, and a commit that fails them publishes nothing.
A sidebar assistant that edits the graph in plain language — add nodes, connect them, set prompts, and queue a run.
A single container with no queue, no cache tier and no companion services to stand up beside it. Run it locally the same way it runs in production.
A single key authenticates every endpoint, and usage meters to the organization it belongs to. Spend is attributed in one place instead of once per service.
A single long-lived HTTP response carries every update, so nothing special has to sit in front of it. The browser notices a dropped network and reconnects on its own.
A single pass on one laptop, reproducible by one command. It establishes a floor; it is not a service level under load.
A single pass on one laptop, reproducible by one command. Read it as a floor that has been established rather than as a service level.
A single turn reaches {turn}; a three-turn window reaches {window} at three times the tokens — {points} points for a decision nobody reports.
A skill is a markdown file

A skill is a markdown file about one thing — Postgres query plans, Zig comptime, TLS certificate chains. Install the plugin and your agent reads the right one when the work calls for it, instead of carrying all of them into every session.
A small free allowance on the new account. With your key, GET {tier} says what it allows and what is left.
A small free allowance on the new account; GET /v1/billing/tier says what it allows and what is left.
A small set of orthogonal, predictable features covers a large solution space.
A social ad for maxpower: a story, a post and a short video.
A soft decline is often a fact about one processor, not about the card. Failed attempts fall through to a backup automatically, and the customer sees one outcome.
A spike on a chart is the start of a question, not the end. Click it and you are in the traces for that window, because they were never in a different system.
A spreadsheet can hold these numbers. It cannot tell you what they become at the next price.
A stable API boundary, independent of which backend runs the request.
A stack trace tells you where. The rest of this tells you who, how often, since when, and what they were doing.
A star much heavier than the Sun burns through its fuel, and its core collapses under its own gravity.
A starter for each Hanzo product. Browse, fork, deploy.
A state and its negation answered apart: share of {n} pairs
A state silent on the question, answered between {low} and {high}: share of {n}
A step is settled by what the verifier records — the exit status, the tests, the diff — never by what anything expected.
A still for the launch post?
A store, a retriever, and vector search over both, so an agent recalls the relevant part of a long history instead of replaying all of it.
A story, a post and a video. Volume: max.

A key is told apart from a token by its prefix, so nothing has to guess what it was handed. Tokens are refused outright if they carry an HMAC signature or no algorithm at all, and a refresh token is single-use — presenting a spent one revokes its whole family rather than the one token.
A key, a model name, and a message is the whole first request.
A label is a word on the forge issue, and its colour comes from the word — so it reads the same here and there. Labels are added on the forge; this board does not write them yet.
A lantern-lit street after rain, painted
A laptop or one GPU, with llama.cpp and Metal
A launch banner. Slightly less lightning.

A launch can run as a dry run: it returns the quote and spends nothing. A real launch is metered against the organization as it goes, per provider, so the bill is assembled from the same numbers the quote came from.
A launch image for maxpower. Cinematic, please.
A launch with dryRun returns the price and creates nothing. The same call without it creates the machine, so what you were quoted is what you asked for.
A ledger, a language for writing transactions, and the machinery around them.
A link to your resume: PDF, Google Drive or Dropbox

A list of rectangles is the shape that looks easier and then cannot answer the only question that matters: close a pane, and who gets the space? With a tree the space belongs to the sibling, so closing replaces the split with that sibling and nothing else moves.

A live agent here is a goroutine: it shares one address space with every other, and nothing about it is an isolation boundary. Code that has to be isolated gets a microVM. The goroutine timings are the median of one pass on {machine}. Every figure here is transcribed from the harness's README rather than read from a run file, and each page names the command that prints it.
A live map of every model, agent, and AI workload across your organization. Latency, cost, drift and anomalies, shown as they happen, with alerting and forensic replay.
A local inference endpoint on a port you pick. Point a client at it and the rest of your code does not change.
A local repo, a CI job, a machine you sshed into, a fix at 2am. Same binary, same identity, same commands.

A location is a path — acme, acme/prod, acme/prod/web, and the app or site under that. Access is a grant at a prefix of one. Keeping them apart is the whole design: containment names a resource, it does not hand every ancestor's members the child.
A log that is not a second copy of the leak
A long context, for large codebases and long documents.
A machine belongs to one org and is named within it. Every read and every terminate is checked against the org on your token, not against the id in the URL.
A machine can carry an agent
A machine is a machine. The provider is a field on it.
A machine that stays up because something is calling it.

A message is redelivered until a consumer acknowledges it. Publishers that stamp a message id get duplicates collapsed inside a window — two minutes unless you say otherwise. Ack every message, ack a sequence to cover everything below it, or ask for no acks at all when fire-and-forget is what you meant.

A million agents are created, written to disk, and read back. What is counted is the state a {dormant} agent occupies — the row that has to exist for an agent to be resumable at all — the rate at which those rows can be written, and the time to bring one back. Nothing is running while the measurement is taken, which is the point: an agent platform’s floor is what it costs to keep an agent that is doing nothing.

A resource has a path: organization, then workspace, then project, then whatever sits under those. A grant covers a path and everything below it. One check asks whether some grant the caller holds covers the target and admits the verb — and org-wide access, one workspace, an invite-only project, and a narrowed credential handed to an agent all fall out of that with no special case for any of them.
A resource tree, not a pile of flags
A resume is a PDF, DOC or DOCX file.
A resume is at most 10 MB.

A retained record — a relationship, a transaction, the assessment behind a case, a refusal — carries its own five-year clock, started by the end of the relationship, by the occasional transaction, or by the refusal itself. Disposal runs daily and proves what it destroyed before it reports it. Alerts and case timelines are durable, and are not on that clock.
A rising timestamp compresses as deltas. A repeated label compresses as a dictionary. A general-purpose compressor runs over whatever is left.
A role is granted at a place — an organization, a workspace under it, a single project. The token carries the one that applies to the request, so your service decides without asking us anything.
A row in a column store rather than a series in a store of its own.
A row is a run, as of its date.

A row marked {ran} is a number produced by our own harness, and the link goes to the run. A row marked {published} is each vendor’s own claim, taken from the page linked and dated the day it was read — we relay those, we did not verify them, and they are their numbers and not ours. Where a vendor has not published something the cell says {unpublished} rather than being left blank, because a blank reads as zero.
A row store reads the whole row to answer a question about two of its fields. A column store reads the two.
A run is a record, not a goroutine. Step state is written down as it goes, so a crash, a deploy or a rescheduled pod resumes where it stopped rather than starting over or losing the run.
A run that survives the restart
A run’s reproducible record, and the rules that govern it.
A sales rep if you want one.

A sandbox is what an agent needs to run a command. What it costs to keep an agent that is doing nothing is {dormant}, and what a running agent holds is {live}. The three are separate measurements with separate commands and they do not add up into a single number.
A sandbox that runs a shell, cold
A saved query you want watched rather than looked at. Same definition as the widget beside it, kept in one place so the alert and the chart cannot disagree.
A school wants seats for every teacher and asks about a discount. I drafted a reply.
A score that is not confident gives the call back to the rules.
A screen, a way to watch it, and the tools the model drives it with

A second LoCoMo harness, in Go, with no language model anywhere in it: lexical retrieval and a fixed extractive reader, with retrieval scoped to the person a question names, against a flat index. Its numbers are on their own scale, not the engine’s.
A second factor is an authenticator app, a code by SMS or email, or a passkey. Adding or dropping one signs the account out of every other browser.

A second factor is an authenticator app, or a code by SMS or email, with recovery codes shown once and stored hashed. Adding one, removing one, or changing which is preferred drops every other session and clears the remember-me window. A session that outlives the change is the same as not having made it.
A secret is a value under a path, a name and an environment, inside one organization. That is the whole model.
A folder tree rather than a single file, shared as one link. Diligence is forty documents and a hundred questions, and both sides need to know what is in scope.
A fork, and it says so
A framework scoped to your engagement
A free Hanzo account opens it, and you come straight back here. The person who shared it will see that you opened it.

A freshly built binary is slower the first time it runs, and not slightly: three fresh builds read 202, 210 and 201 ns, and the same three read 123, 125 and 123 ns when run again. The goroutines did not get cheaper. The window is 41 ms rather than 25 ms for the same 200,000 spawns, so it is one fixed cost inside the measurement, paid once per binary for first-touch paging and the kernel's signature check on first exec. Divided by 200,000 and printed per goroutine, it is the cost of starting the program wearing the name of the thing being measured. This page read 187 ns for exactly that reason; the harness now runs the round twice and reports the second.
A function can request an NVIDIA GPU and be scheduled onto a node that has one. That is what lets model work be a function instead of a service somebody has to keep alive.

A function is a record in a collection, so the collection’s rules decide who may run it. It runs in-process with two calls bound — read a record, read a list — and no network, no filesystem, no shell. Whatever the first version binds is supported forever, which is why that list is short.
A fund Theo knows from his last company
A gateway here, an agent runtime there, a policy layer, a tracer, a GPU contract. Each is one more integration to keep alive. On Hanzo they are one runtime.
A gateway is a small skill whose whole job is to notice. Say Postgres and discover-database wakes up; say comptime and discover-zig does. It pulls the specific files and gets out of the way.
A glider is five cells. Collide enough of them and you can build a computer. We are building AI the same way: small parts with one job each, made to be combined.
A goroutine is not a sandbox.
A grant is matched exactly, not by prefix

A grant on acme/prod does not cover acme/production. What stops it is an exact match against a known set rather than a prefix walk — a plain string prefix test would admit the second, which is a read across two tenants. An empty path covers nothing, so a scope that arrived missing or malformed denies rather than matching everything.

A group's committed offsets live in a PubSub key-value bucket, so a consumer that dies comes back where it left off instead of at the top. Ask for an offset that has aged out and you get OFFSET_OUT_OF_RANGE, so the client resets rather than hangs.
A handler file, a trigger, and the cluster you already run
A hop, or no hop at all
A job carries a priority, so the urgent one goes ahead of the backlog. Inside one priority it stays first in, first out, which is what keeps ordinary work from quietly starving.
A job that needs cards for hours and nothing for the rest of the week.
A job that runs out of attempts lands in the failed set carrying its error and stack. Read it, fix the cause, retry it. Nothing disappears because it went wrong.

A joint-embedding predictive architecture does not reconstruct pixels. It predicts the embedding of a piece of an image from the embedding of another piece — so the model spends its capacity on what the image means rather than on what it looks like. Jin is our work on that idea, in the open, with the code and the papers to read.
A key for the API, Bedrock, or Vertex
A key from the console reaches the RPC endpoints, the token and NFT data, the wallets and the webhooks. Pick a chain and read something. No credit card required.
A binary in your own network. Whatever you decide not to forward, you decide before the data has left — which is the only point where that is still your call.
A birthday card for Theo, in the house style
A bot can start background runs that work in parallel and post what they found back in the chat that asked.
A bot that waters the plants.
A bounded choice with known options — Kai answers with calibrated odds.
A bounded decision has edges. Move the evidence or the risk and watch the answer cross the line — and read the smallest change that would cross it.
A brand with regional shops, or an agency running stores for clients. Stores are scoped by organisation and can price the same product differently.

A browser cannot put a header on the request that opens a stream. So you mint a short-lived grant on an ordinary authenticated call and spend it once, within thirty seconds — rather than putting a token that opens every service into a URL that every proxy and access log will keep.

A bucket is a stream that keeps the last value per key, so you get watches, per-key history and expiry from the same server and the same connection. It is where Hanzo Stream keeps its consumer offsets.
A bug report becomes a pull request; a person reviews it, the checks pass, and it ships, all in the channel.
A build ends at a published image. What runs where is declared separately, and applied from that declaration.
A build is running from the last commit on main.
A call the cheap preset can answer does not spend the flagship.
A calm voice reading the shop sign aloud
A card is a forge issue — moving it here moves it there.
A card's dates come from its forge milestone, which is why they read here and cannot yet be set here.
A cart is a real object with its own id, so someone can leave and come back, and you can look at what they left in it.
A channel for each team and project, direct messages, and threads that keep a decision next to the question that started it.
A chat that does the work, not just the talking
A choice, a score or a yes/no, each with its probabilities, for agent loops such as Hanzo Dev's.

A clean implementation of the image variant: a context encoder, a target encoder that is its moving average, and a predictor that has to guess the target embeddings. Both a ViT and an energy-transformer backbone.
A code to the address before the document opens. Otherwise a forwarded link is a stranger, and your analytics are counting the wrong person.
A coding agent that opens the files, makes the change, runs the tests and shows you the diff.
A cold prompt of about that many tokens on a quiet box, measured {day}: {box}; {model}.

A collection is a real table with a schema you write down. The moment it exists it answers over HTTP, carries an access rule, streams its changes, and shows up in the admin. There is no code generation step and nothing to wire together.
A column store for analytical SQL
A command palette reaches every module and every record without learning where anything lives. The sidebar is yours to reorder and prune.
A commit to the forge starts the build.
A comparison reads rows of one benchmark and one metric. These are {rows}.
A compatible inference interface for chat, completions, embeddings, multimodal models and agent workloads.
A complete payment gateway bridging fiat and crypto. Accept stablecoins, process card payments, enable on/off-ramps, and handle compliance—all through a single API.
A completion from any model your organization can reach, streamed or buffered. Model ids come from the catalog, so the list is a request rather than a page in the docs.

A million dormant agents written to disk and read back: 477 bytes of state each, 455 MB for the million, and a resume in 0.034 ms. Measured on a laptop, against a competitor figure that was modelled and never billed.
A model trained on your own events, with the search over model shape that finds which one to use.
A model writes the edit, asked for as a strict schema.
A modular feedback architecture, not a claim of unattended production self-modification. Only candidates that meet the relevant evaluation and release gates are promoted.
A module per product, one shell around them
A multi-step routine can stop at the steps you mark and wait for your yes before it goes on.

GPQA-Diamond is four-way multiple choice on settled science. It measures what a pool knows and rewards a router that recognises a hard question; it says nothing about whether the answer is reasoned, whether the model holds up over a long autonomous run, or whether it can use a tool. The routing overhead is real work this table does not score either.

GPQA-Diamond is the hardest subset of GPQA: 198 multiple-choice questions in biology, physics and chemistry, written by domain PhDs and filtered to the ones that other PhDs get right and skilled non-experts get wrong even with the web open. It is a knowledge benchmark rather than an agentic one — one question, one answer, no tools — which is what makes it useful here: it isolates the choice of model from everything else a system does.

A freshly built binary is slower the first time it runs, and not slightly: three fresh builds read 202, 210 and 201 ns, and the same three read 123, 125 and 123 ns when run again. The goroutines did not get cheaper. The window is 41 ms rather than 25 ms for the same 200,000 spawns, so it is one fixed cost inside the measurement, paid once per binary for first-touch paging and the kernel's signature check on first exec. Divided by 200,000 and printed per goroutine, it is the cost of starting the program wearing the name of the thing being measured. GPQA-Diamond is the hardest subset of GPQA: 198 multiple-choice questions in biology, physics and chemistry, written by domain PhDs and filtered to the ones that other PhDs get right and skilled non-experts get wrong even with the web open. 601 bytes against a 128 MB container floor is about 223,000×, and against a V8 isolate about 1,745× — and that second one is a goroutine against a JavaScript VM, so read it as what each primitive costs rather than as one beating the other. A freshly built binary is slower the first time it runs, and not slightly: three fresh builds read 202, 210 and 201 ns, and the same three read 123, 125 and 123 ns when run again. The goroutines did not get cheaper. The window is 41 ms rather than 25 ms for the same 200,000 spawns, so it is one fixed cost inside the measurement, paid once per binary for first-touch paging and the kernel's signature check on first exec. Divided by 200,000 and printed per goroutine, it is the cost of starting the program wearing the name of the thing being measured. This page read 187 ns for exactly that reason; the harness now runs the round twice and reports the second.

601 bytes against a 128 MB container floor is about 223,000×, and against a V8 isolate about 1,745× — and that second one is a goroutine against a JavaScript VM, so read it as what each primitive costs rather than as one beating the other. The isolate column is measured here rather than cited: a fresh isolated-vm isolate is 1.00 MiB and 0.35 ms on this laptop, close to the 1.2 MB attributed to it, because a megabyte is what any isolate costs including one of ours. The number that matters more for an interactive system is the 125 ns: an agent that costs nothing to start does not need to be kept warm, and a pool is a thing you maintain because starting was expensive.
